title: AMD's 12GW pledge stays gigawatts, not customer-filed dollars/racks, by Q1 2027
body: AMD walks into Thursday's keynote with a headline the tape has already paid for: OpenAI and Meta are reported to have committed a combined twelve gigawatts of AMD capacity, with Microsoft anchoring Helios and Oracle taking MI450 into OCI. The prediction is that this figure stays what it is today - a power-denominated number carried on AMD's and the press's authority - and does not convert, on any customer's own authority, into a dollar value or a rack or GPU count by the end of Q1 2027. Gigawatts are an elastic planning unit: earmarked datacenter power, staged over years and conditioned on availability, not a signed silicon order. The keynote will ship roadmap, availability windows and logos; what it cannot manufacture is a named buyer putting a countable commercial number behind Helios in its own checkable disclosure. The gap holds because hyperscalers report capex in aggregate and never itemize a chip vendor, and the larger named party, OpenAI, is private and files nothing. It matters because a run to roughly $553 - near a double on the year, with sell-side targets toward $700 - rests on the twelve-gigawatt roster reading as money-good; if the market later demands customer-filed dollars or racks and none appear, the premium is what unwinds. The falsifier is clean: if OpenAI, Meta, Microsoft or Oracle quantifies its AMD Helios or MI450 commitment as a dollar value or a rack or GPU count inside its own earnings call, 8-K, 10-Q or first-party capex statement before Q1 2027 closes, the prediction fails.

reasoning.because: OpenAI and Meta are reported committing ~12GW to AMD, a figure no customer has itself quantified
reasoning.given: Hyperscalers report capex in aggregate, not by chip vendor; OpenAI is private and files nothing
reasoning.so_that: The 12GW headline can lift AMD toward $700 yet never surface as a checkable dollar or rack figure from any buyer
reasoning.landing: By Q1 2027 no named buyer files an AMD Helios dollar, rack or GPU figure
reasoning.plain_language: AMD says two giant customers promised huge computing power. But those customers probably won't put a real dollar or order number on it soon.

summary: Pre-keynote reporting pins OpenAI and Meta at a combined 12GW of AMD capacity. The prediction: that figure stays a headline and, by Q1 2027, no named buyer converts it into a customer-filed dollar value or rack/GPU count, since hyperscalers report capex in aggregate and OpenAI is private.
